name: Palestine

fees.name: ETA-IL (Israel Electronic Travel Authorization, required to reach the West Bank via Israeli-controlled borders)
fees.validity: Up to 2 years or passport expiry; stays up to 90 days per entry
fees.applies: Nationals of Israel's visa-exempt countries (USA, GBR, CAN, EU, etc.)
fees.notes: Palestine issues no entry visas of its own; all access to the West Bank (Ben Gurion Airport, Allenby/King Hussein Bridge) is controlled by Israel. Mandatory since 1 Jan 2025; fee non-refundable, paid online by card.

fees.name: Israel B/2 visitor visa (consular sticker visa, required for non-visa-exempt nationalities to transit Israel into the West Bank)
fees.validity: Up to 3 months from date of issue
fees.applies: Nationalities not visa-exempt for Israel (incl. IND, CHN, NGA, PAK, PHL, BGD, RUS)
fees.notes: Fee is set per Israeli mission in local currency (e.g. CAD 33 at the Montreal consulate); no single global amount published, so amount left null. Verify with the local Israeli embassy fee chart.

vfs.note: The Palestinian Authority operates no visa system or outsourced application centres. Israeli B/2 visas are lodged directly with Israeli embassies/consulates (some missions use local appointment providers, but no published VFS/TLS/BLS fee applies to Palestine).

free_visa_notes: Palestine itself charges no visa fee and issues no entry visas: border control for the West Bank is exercised by Israel (Gaza access is separately controlled and currently closed to tourism). Travellers pay Israel's fees instead - ETA-IL NIS 25 for visa-exempt nationals, or an Israeli B/2 consular visa (fee varies by mission) for others. Entry via Allenby Bridge from Jordan also runs under Israeli control.
